rows.name: Audit report content
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 6.5.1 covers preparing the audit report, which provides a complete, accurate, concise and clear record of the audit including its scope, criteria, findings and conclusions.

rows.name: Determining a nonconformity
rows.description: Establishing that a specific requirement exists, that evidence relates to it, and that the evidence shows the requirement is not fulfilled. All three are needed before a finding is a nonconformity.

rows.name: Process importance as a factor
rows.description: The importance of the processes concerned is a named input to programme establishment under ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2.2, and drives which areas receive more frequent or deeper audit.

rows.name: The risk treatment process
rows.description: Clause 6.1.3 requires selecting treatment options, determining all necessary controls, comparing them with Annex A, producing the Statement of Applicability, formulating a treatment plan, and obtaining risk owners approval.

rows.name: Third-party audit
rows.description: An audit conducted by an independent auditing organization, such as a body providing certification of conformity, or by a regulatory authority. Governed by ISO/IEC 17021-1, not by ISO 19011.

rows.name: Competence under clause 7.2
rows.description: Requires determining necessary competence, ensuring persons are competent on the basis of education, training or experience, taking action where applicable and evaluating its effectiveness, and retaining documented information as evidence of competence.

rows.name: Verifying corrective action
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 10.2 d) requires the effectiveness of any corrective action taken to be reviewed - which requires evidence of the changed arrangement operating, not evidence that it was made.

rows.name: When to bring a technical expert
rows.description: Where a conclusion would require technical knowledge the audit team does not hold, the choice is to engage an expert, narrow the conclusion, or record the limitation - not to proceed on assumption.

rows.name: Degree of verification
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 6.4.7 states that only information subject to some degree of verification should be accepted as audit evidence. Verification is a matter of degree, not a binary test.

rows.name: Reliability of electronic evidence
rows.description: Electronically presented information can be filtered, edited or generated between the source system and the auditor's view, so the auditor evaluates what the presentation establishes rather than what it appears to show.

rows.name: Controls over a non-deterministic process
rows.description: A control validated against a process producing consistent output may not hold when the same process produces varying output, because the evidence of effectiveness was drawn from a behaviour that no longer applies.

rows.name: Risk assessment and treatment in operation
rows.description: Clause 8.2 requires assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur; clause 8.3 requires the treatment plan to be implemented. Both require documented information of the results.

rows.name: Second-party audit
rows.description: An audit conducted by a party with an interest in the organization, such as a customer, or by another party on their behalf - including audits an organization conducts on its own external providers.

rows.name: First-party audit
rows.description: An audit conducted by or on behalf of the organization on its own management system, to inform the organization about its own conformity and effectiveness. It produces no certificate and serves no external party.

rows.name: The risk assessment process
rows.description: Clause 6.1.2 requires a defined and applied process that establishes risk criteria, produces consistent, valid and comparable results, identifies risks and risk owners, analyses consequences and likelihood, and evaluates against the criteria.

rows.name: Audit requirements diverge
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2.2 a) requires audit criteria and scope; ISO/IEC 42001 requires objectives, criteria and scope. ISO/IEC 27001 reports results to relevant management; ISO/IEC 42001 to relevant managers.

rows.name: Compliance against conformity
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.8 Note 1 records that where the audit criteria are legal, statutory or regulatory requirements, the words compliance and non-compliance are often used in a finding rather than conformity language.

rows.name: The information security policy
rows.description: Clause 5.2 requires the policy to be appropriate to the organization's purpose, to include objectives or provide the framework for setting them, and to include commitments to satisfy applicable requirements and to continual improvement.

rows.name: Human review as a control
rows.description: Where review of AI output is claimed as the control, its effectiveness depends on whether the reviewer has the information, time and authority to reject - which is what the auditor tests, not whether the review step exists.

rows.name: Competence to use an AI audit tool
rows.description: Understanding what an AI-based tool does to the evidence it processes, what it leaves unverified, and when its use changes what the audit can conclude. Annex A.16 adds the technical skills to use the technology itself.

rows.name: The risk-based audit programme
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.8 states the risk-based approach should substantively influence the planning and implementation of the audit programme, so that audits focus on matters significant to the audit client and to the programme objectives.

rows.name: Monitoring and measurement
rows.description: Clause 9.1 requires the organization to determine six things: what needs monitoring and measuring including processes and controls, the methods, when performed, who shall monitor and measure, when results are analysed and evaluated, and who shall analyse and evaluate.

rows.name: Correction against corrective action
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 10.2 a) requires action to control and correct the nonconformity and deal with the consequences; clause 10.2 b) requires evaluating the need for action to eliminate the causes. Neither term is defined inside ISO/IEC 27001.

rows.name: Objective evidence is not audit evidence
rows.description: Two distinct defined terms. Objective evidence (3.9) is data supporting the existence or verity of something; audit evidence (3.10) is objective evidence that is relevant to the audit criteria and verifiable. The clause 3.1 definition of audit uses the former.

rows.name: Objectives are practice, not a 27001 requirement
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2.2 a) requires the organization to define the audit criteria and scope for each audit. It does not require audit objectives. ISO/IEC 42001's own 9.2.2 a) adds objectives where ISO/IEC 27001 does not.

rows.name: Interested party climate requirements
rows.description: Amendment 1:2024 adds NOTE 2 at the end of clause 4.2: relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change. It is a second note - the existing note on legal, regulatory and contractual requirements becomes NOTE 1. A note is not a requirement.

rows.name: Operational planning and control
rows.description: Clause 8.1 requires the organization to plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements and implement the clause 6 actions, by establishing criteria and controlling the processes in accordance with them, with documented information available to have confidence the processes ran as planned.

rows.name: ICT and emerging technology competence
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 7.2.3 item 10 requires auditors to understand the appropriateness and consequences of using information and communications technology tools, and emerging technology, to conduct audits. The requirement is general: it covers remote-audit tooling, sampling and analysis software, and whatever arrives next.

rows.name: Review Feedback Craft
rows.description: Specific, kind, actionable feedback.

rows.name: Plan-Implement-Test-Review
rows.description: The agentic loop's stages.

rows.name: Review/Integration Debt
rows.description: Debt from generation outpacing verification.

rows.name: Surface Debt (Transparency)
rows.description: Making debt visible and negotiating paydown.

rows.name: Developer Owns Verification
rows.description: The Developer owns verification, not the tool.

rows.name: Skill Atrophy Risk
rows.description: Over-reliance on AI can erode fundamentals.

rows.name: Code Review
rows.description: A collaboration practice that spreads ownership and quality.

rows.name: Resist Command-and-Control
rows.description: Guarding self-management against re-imposed task assignment.

rows.name: The Developers' Event
rows.description: For and by the Developers, not a status report.

rows.name: Empirical Process
rows.description: Empiricism as the basis for engineering decisions under uncertainty.

rows.name: Velocity Outpacing Verification
rows.description: AI output arriving faster than it can be verified.

rows.name: Refinement is not a Scrum event
rows.description: Common misconception clarified.

rows.name: Empirical process control
rows.description: Knowledge from experience and decisions from observation.

rows.name: Empirical vs predictive process
rows.description: Choosing between iterative and plan-driven approaches.

rows.name: Coaching the organization
rows.description: SM serves the organization through training and coaching.

rows.name: Artifact transparency
rows.description: Artifacts must be visible to support inspection and adaptation.

rows.name: Refinement as activity (not event)
rows.description: Ongoing activity; not one of the five Scrum events.

rows.name: Scrum Master serves the organization
rows.description: Leading, training, coaching Scrum adoption; planning implementations; removing barriers.

rows.name: Scrum Master accountability for team effectiveness
rows.description: The central accountability of the Scrum Master per 2020 Guide.

rows.name: Sprint Review
rows.description: Event to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog.

rows.name: Review bottleneck
rows.description: An impediment in which AI generates output faster than the team can inspect it, so review — not creation — becomes the constraint on flow.

rows.name: Artifact integrity
rows.description: An artifact that is maintained but no longer truthful.

rows.name: Transparency erosion
rows.description: Transparency lost gradually rather than by any single decision.

rows.name: Event purpose
rows.description: Each Scrum event exists to enable a specific inspection and adaptation.

rows.name: Transparency test
rows.description: Assessing whether an artifact still provides the information its commitment promises.

rows.name: Review as presentation
rows.description: A Sprint Review reduced to a one-way demonstration that changes nothing.

rows.name: Risk containment
rows.description: Sprint length limits risk of cost and effort to a smaller time frame.

rows.name: Review degradation
rows.description: A Sprint Review that has stopped inspecting because there is too much to inspect.

rows.name: Service to the organization
rows.description: The Scrum Master helps employees and stakeholders understand and enact an empirical approach for complex work.

rows.name: Consequence threshold
rows.description: A derived threshold for intervention: whether the consequence would cost the Sprint Goal or a usable Increment.

rows.name: Developer-owned event
rows.description: The Daily Scrum belongs to the Developers; others attend only if actively working on Sprint Backlog items.

rows.name: Sprint Review
rows.description: A working session where the Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect the outcome and adapt the Product Backlog.

rows.name: Stakeholder Transparency
rows.description: Being transparent with stakeholders about progress.

rows.name: Transparency, Inspection, Adaptation
rows.description: The three empirical pillars of Scrum.

rows.name: Feature Waiter Anti-Pattern
rows.description: The order-taker PO who only relays requests.

rows.name: Refinement Is Not an Event
rows.description: An ongoing activity, not a formal Scrum event.

rows.name: Review Is Not a Demo
rows.description: A working session, not a one-way demo.

rows.name: Transparency Breakdown
rows.description: Detecting and correcting low transparency in the backlog.

rows.name: Transparency for Agents
rows.description: Transparency now serves machines as well as people.

rows.name: Artifact Transparency
rows.description: Artifacts must be transparent for inspection to be meaningful.

rows.name: Sprint Review
rows.description: Inspecting the Increment and adapting the backlog with stakeholders.
